confirmed_findings.evidence: Opening says Series concatenated by rows align by Index. pd.concat(axis=0) stacks along the index axis and can preserve duplicate labels; it does not reconcile labels like Series arithmetic.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can expect row concat to reconcile duplicate business labels and silently build wrong reconciliation logic.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Separate Series arithmetic alignment, concat(axis=0) stacking and concat(axis=1) alignment.

confirmed_findings.evidence: cliente_id is promoted as stable business Index while the gate covers transactions, where client ids legitimately repeat. pandas Index labels need not be unique.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can treat repeated client ids in a transaction table as invalid duplicate rows or lose the true transaction row identity.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use cliente_id as Index only for one-row-per-client data; transactions keep transaction_id or RangeIndex and cliente_id as a column.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Schema is defined as the set/map of dtypes while later claims assign it required-column and shape responsibilities.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can call a dtype map a complete schema and assume nullability, uniqueness/ranges/required columns are covered.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Call it a minimum ingestion schema: required columns plus dtype/coercion policy; deeper constraints arrive in S16.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Lesson says mixing a number and a name becomes object and seeing object in expected text means source mixed types. object can be explicitly requested or contain arbitrary Python objects; mixed CSV inference is parser/chunk dependent.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can diagnose object dtype as proof of source corruption or assume every mixed-looking column must become object.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach object as a generic Python-object container; diagnose mixed inference from values/parser warnings and declared contract, not dtype alone.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Gate requires row/column reconciliation; theory only prints len(df)=2 and never compares expected_rows or required_columns.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Printing a row count can be mistaken for reconciliation while missing/extra rows or columns pass.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Compare observed vs expected rows and required columns immediately after parsing, with explicit failure evidence.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Target is pandas 3 but lesson repeatedly frames the issue as SettingWithCopy/SettingWithCopyWarning. pandas 3 removed that warning; chained assignment never updates parent under CoW and emits ChainedAssignmentError as a warning.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner on target version can look for a warning that no longer exists and infer the pattern is safe when it is absent.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use pandas-3 CoW/ChainedAssignmentError terminology and one-step .loc assignment.

confirmed_findings.evidence: CoW is glossed as 'escritura sobre copia automática', suggesting eager physical copying.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner conflates API isolation with eager copying and transfers wrong memory/view reasoning from NumPy.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say derived objects behave independently at the API while pandas may share memory and defer physical copying until a write.

confirmed_findings.evidence: errors='coerce' is called preferable to failing the batch if failures are counted.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can universalize coercion+continue to critical identifiers/amounts that policy should reject or quarantine.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Frame coercion+report as a lab policy; critical fields may require rejection/quarantine under the data contract.

confirmed_findings.evidence: schema dict is created but never iterated or used; conversions are hardcoded separately.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Adding a schema entry changes nothing while learner believes schema drives behavior.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Implement apply_schema that checks required columns and applies every schema entry, returning (df, report).

confirmed_findings.evidence: Roadmap requires CSV/Parquet/Excel, but theory never writes/reads Parquet and substitutes a dtype dict named parquet_contract.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can claim Parquet competence without exercising engine dependency, Parquet bytes or round-trip type preservation.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add a real optional Parquet round-trip with pyarrow/fastparquet; if unavailable, mark that gate not run rather than treating CSV+schema as equivalent.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Manifest source is only synthetic_clientes_v1 and content_sha256 hashes output CSV, not input source bytes or parser/schema configuration.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Reviewer cannot reconstruct what exact input bytes/config produced an output; different inputs/settings can share the same output provenance record.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Record input source/path, full input SHA-256, parser/schema version/options, coercion report, then output path/hash/shape separately.

confirmed_findings.evidence: content_sha256 stores hexdigest()[:12], a 12-hex prefix, while field name implies complete SHA-256.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can rely on a short display fingerprint as a full artifact identifier.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Store full digest as content_sha256 and optionally a separately named sha256_prefix.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Lesson says Parquet stores first all client_id then all monto then all region. Actual hierarchy is file -> row groups -> one column chunk per column in each row group -> pages.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner imagines one whole-file block per column and misunderstands row-group IO/statistics.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach the actual file/row-group/column-chunk/page hierarchy first.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Projection pushdown is described as not something you activate, merely a consequence of layout; filter pruning is similarly presented. Layout enables skipping, but the reader/query engine must request columns/predicates and exploit metadata.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can believe choosing Parquet automatically avoids reading unused columns/row groups regardless of read API/query plan.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say Parquet enables pushdown; reader/engine must receive selected columns/filter and use metadata. Demonstrate with a real columns/filter read when engine exists.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Text says row format forces all other 39 values to be read even if discarded. CSV reader must scan row text but usecols can avoid materializing unnecessary columns; exact work is parser-dependent.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner turns format comparison into a false absolute rule and misses parser-level projection.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Distinguish scanning row-oriented text from materializing/parsing selected columns.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Lesson says boolean filters live inside loc. df[mask] is valid for read-only selection; the critical danger is chained assignment on writes.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner misclassifies valid filtering as unsafe and fails to identify the actual mutation hazard.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Prefer loc for explicit row+column selection/mutation but acknowledge df[mask] is valid read-only filtering.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Opening says merge and join(on=...) combine on named columns and Index does not participate. DataFrame.join(on=...) matches caller column(s) to the other object's Index; join defaults to index-on-index when on is omitted.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can expect right.cliente_id column to be used by join(on='cliente_id') while pandas actually uses the right Index.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach merge(on=...) as column-oriented; teach DataFrame.join separately as index-oriented, including caller-column-to-other-index semantics.

confirmed_findings.evidence: After row-group pruning, lesson moves directly to dataset partitioning and tiny-file tradeoffs, blending row groups inside files with file/directory partitions.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Learner can solve a row-group pruning problem by over-partitioning files and create a small-files problem.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Separate dataset/file partitioning from row groups inside each Parquet file; both can aid pruning but have different controls/trade-offs.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: NumPy te dio velocidad... cada columna necesita su propio tratamiento.
paragraph_audit.improved_version: NumPy te dio velocidad al operar arrays homogéneos. Los archivos tabulares reales mezclan identificadores, montos, fechas y categorías entre columnas; pandas permite dar a cada columna un tipo y una política de conversión propios.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Buen puente S14→S15; precisa heterogeneidad entre columnas.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: dos Series se suman o se concatenan por filas... alinea por Index... join(on=…) Index no interviene
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En aritmética entre Series, pandas alinea etiquetas. concat(axis=0) apila filas y puede conservar etiquetas repetidas; concat(axis=1) alinea etiquetas del otro eje. merge(on='clave') usa columnas; DataFrame.join() es index-oriented y join(on='clave') compara esa columna del izquierdo contra el Index del derecho.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Repara dos modelos de combinación técnicamente falsos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: el conjunto de todos los dtypes es el schema
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Aquí llamaremos schema mínimo de ingesta al mapa de columnas requeridas y su dtype/política de conversión. No expresa todavía unicidad, rangos ni reglas entre columnas; S16 endurece esas restricciones.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Evita vender dtype-map como schema completo.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Un valor ilegible se transforma en faltante... nunca arreglar en silencio
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Cuando esta sección use coerción, un valor ilegible se vuelve missing solo bajo política explícita y el fallo se cuenta. Campos críticos pueden exigir rechazo/cuarentena. Regla común: nunca reparar ni descartar en silencio.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: ¿qué promete cada columna...? index=False salvo clave documentada
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Pregunta guía: ¿qué promete cada columna y qué ocurre cuando no cumple? Lee, tipa, reconcilia y exporta datos sintéticos con evidencia; conserva las claves de negocio como columnas cuando exportes con index=False.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Scope correcto; se hace explícita preservación de keys.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Bloque de referencia...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Bloque de referencia: orden, ritmo, criterio de cierre y dependencias.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: T1 fija... T4 cierra...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: T1 cubre estructuras y lectura; T2 selección/CoW; T3 tipos/coerción/schema mínimo; T4 formatos y provenance.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Ritmo orientativo... 10 horas
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Ritmo orientativo: unas 10 horas, con tres o cuatro para el núcleo y el resto para práctica/proyecto/autochequeo.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Criterio de cierre. Filas reconciliadas...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Criterio de cierre: comparar filas observadas contra esperadas, verificar columnas requeridas, emitir reporte de coerciones y manifest que identifique input y output.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: pandas 3... object queda para columnas que mezclaron tipos
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Dependencias: pandas 3; openpyxl para Excel; pyarrow o fastparquet para Parquet. El texto inferido usa str; string es nullable. object es un contenedor de Python objects y no demuestra por sí solo que el source mezcló tipos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Index... eje de negocio que decide qué filas se combinan
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Index es el eje de etiquetas. En aritmética alinea Series; la llave de combinación depende de merge/join/concat. No es identidad universal del negocio.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Index estable (cliente_id)... id único
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Usa cliente_id como Index solo cuando el contrato sea una fila por cliente. En transacciones, conserva transaction_id como identidad de fila o RangeIndex y deja cliente_id como columna; verifica unicidad solo donde aplique.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: etiqueta ≠ posición
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Conserva la regla: etiqueta ≠ posición; loc selecciona por label e iloc por posición aunque a veces coincidan.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: mezcla número con nombre → object
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En pandas 3 el texto inferido usa str. En archivos grandes/inferencia por chunks, tipos incompatibles pueden producir object/DtypeWarning; no deduzcas la causa solo por dtype. Declara y valida el dtype esperado.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Sustituye causalidad falsa por parser contract.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: encoding, sep, decimal, na_values, required column
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Declara encoding, separador y decimal; usa na_values para marcadores propios y falla con mensaje explícito si falta una columna requerida.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: reconcilia filas vs esperadas...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Después de leer, valida len(df)==expected_rows cuando exista conteo esperado y required_columns <= set(df.columns); registra observado/esperado antes de continuar.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: filtros booleanos viven dentro de loc... SettingWithCopy
paragraph_audit.improved_version: df[mask] es válido para lectura; usa loc[mask, columns] cuando quieras filas+columnas explícitas y para mutación en una sola etapa. En pandas 3 no uses df[mask]['col']=...: no actualiza el padre.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Distingue read selection de write hazard.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: assign devuelve nuevo DataFrame
paragraph_audit.improved_version: assign devuelve un nuevo DataFrame y favorece pipelines legibles; usa query solo bajo convención/test del equipo.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: si solo lees no copies... decide padre o copy
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Si mutas el original, hazlo en una sola operación con loc. Si el subset tendrá vida independiente, crea copy. Bajo CoW el subset se comporta independiente aunque pandas pueda compartir memoria internamente hasta escribir.
paragraph_audit.rationale: Puente CoW sin trasladar NumPy literalmente.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Copy-on-Write — escritura sobre copia automática...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En pandas 3 CoW es el único comportamiento: todo resultado de indexación se comporta como independiente del original; pandas puede compartir memoria y copiar al escribir. Chained assignment nunca actualiza el padre.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: un solo loc o copy explícita
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Para modificar el original usa una sola asignación loc; para un subset independiente usa copy y muta ese objeto.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: assign/where... alias c=df
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Métodos que devuelven objeto nuevo reducen mutación accidental; c=df es alias, no copia.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: object... verlo significa archivo mezcló tipos
paragraph_audit.improved_version: str es texto inferido en pandas 3; string es StringDtype nullable. object puede almacenar Python objects y su presencia no identifica una causa única: valida contenido/contrato.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: errors='coerce' preferible a tumbar todo lote
paragraph_audit.improved_version: En este laboratorio coerce+report permite estudiar fallos; campos críticos pueden requerir rechazo/cuarentena. La política debe estar declarada por columna.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: fallos de conversión, no nulo parser
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Reporta conversiones que crean nuevos missing y sepáralas de nulos que ya venían del parser.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: schema dict... archivo cambia y schema avisa
paragraph_audit.improved_version: El schema mínimo se vuelve contrato solo cuando una función comprueba required columns y aplica dtype/coerción para cada entrada; el dict aislado es documentación.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: delta de NaN antes/después
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Separa nulos de origen de fallos nuevos de coerción y falla explicablemente ante columnas requeridas ausentes.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: reporte viaja junto DataFrame (df, report)
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Haz que apply_schema(raw, schema) devuelva (df_tipado, report) y que añadir una nueva entrada al schema cambie realmente la validación/conversión.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: si no hay Parquet, CSV+schema... aprendizaje es el mismo
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Parquet requiere motor y round-trip real. CSV+schema es fallback documentado, no evidencia equivalente de Parquet.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: index=False... round-trip columns
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Usa index=False si keys siguen como columnas; en round-trip compara columnas requeridas y, cuando aplique, dtypes/valores críticos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: dict parquet_contract aunque no haya pyarrow
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Si hay motor, escribe/relee Parquet y valida schema; si falta, marca parquet_roundtrip:not_run_missing_engine y entrega CSV+schema como fallback, sin llamarlo Parquet completado.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: manifest... provenance source + hash artefacto
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Manifest distingue input y output: input source/hash + parser/schema/coerciones → output rows/columns/dtypes/path/hash.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: SHA-256 truncado del CSV
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Guarda SHA-256 completo como output_sha256; usa un campo separado output_sha256_prefix solo para display.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: source=... + content_sha256 corto = evidencia auditable
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Incluye input_source/input_sha256/parser_options/schema_version/coercion_report/rows/columns/dtypes/memory/output_path/output_sha256.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Parquet guarda primero todos los ids, luego montos...
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Parquet: file → row groups → un column chunk por columna dentro de cada row group → pages. Esa jerarquía permite selective IO.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: projection pushdown no es una opción que actives
paragraph_audit.improved_version: CSV debe recorrer el texto de filas aunque usecols reduzca materialización. Parquet permite localizar column chunks; hay projection pushdown cuando reader/engine recibe columnas y empuja esa selección a la lectura física.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: min/max → filter pushdown/pruning
paragraph_audit.improved_version: Un reader con filtro compatible puede usar estadísticas de row groups para descartarlos. Esto es distinto de particionar un dataset en archivos/directorios.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: partición... muchos archivos diminutos... Arrow memoria
paragraph_audit.improved_version: La eficacia del pruning depende de estadísticas útiles; ordenar/agrupar puede ayudar. Separadamente, particionar en demasiados archivos crea small-file overhead. Parquet describe almacenamiento; Arrow, representación columnar en memoria.

technical_validation.local_runtime_note: Local private Python had pandas 2.2.3 plus a pyarrow compatibility problem, so it was not used as authority for pandas-3 semantics. Target-version claims were checked against current pandas 3.0.x documentation.
official_checks: CoW is the only pandas-3 behavior and chained assignment never updates the parent
SettingWithCopyWarning was removed; ChainedAssignmentError is the warning class
join(on=...) matches caller column(s) to other Index
Index labels need not be unique
Parquet contains row groups with column chunks

adversarial_questions.question: If Index is business identity, what happens when one client has many transactions?
adversarial_questions.verdict: Current model overgeneralizes; row labels and domain identity must be separated.

adversarial_questions.question: If schema is executable, does adding a third schema entry change theory behavior?
adversarial_questions.verdict: No; canonical code ignores schema and hardcodes conversions.

adversarial_questions.question: If no Parquet bytes are written/read, can a dtype dict prove the Parquet outcome?
adversarial_questions.verdict: No; it exercises neither Parquet IO nor preservation.

priority_repairs: Repair provenance input→config→output with full hashes
S16_entry_watchlist: Do not inherit schema-driven ingestion as USABLE
Do not assume executable row/column reconciliation
Do not infer source mixed types from object dtype alone
Use pandas-3 CoW/ChainedAssignmentError semantics, not SettingWithCopyWarning
Do not assume a Parquet round-trip exists
Do not treat S15 manifest as sufficient lineage
Keep client identity separate from transaction row identity
Do not treat pushdown as automatic merely because storage is Parquet
